title: Invert Binary Tree
description: Swap each node’s left and right children recursively — the mirror image of the original tree.

notes: Pure recursive swap — recurse first, then assign, so children are independently inverted before the swap.
Base case `if (!root) return null` covers empty trees and terminates at leaf children.
O(n) time, O(h) space; h = O(log n) balanced, O(n) skewed.

questions.q: What does invertTree do at every node?
options: Swaps the left and right children
root is a leaf — return root
root.left and root.right both null — return 0

questions.q: Space complexity of the recursive version (call stack)?
options: O(h) where h is the tree height

exercises.prompt: Fill in the recursive swap; inorder traversal of the inverted BST should be sorted DESC.

blanks.hint: new right = inverted ORIGINAL left (saved in tmp)

L3.prompt: Write `invertTree(root)` that swaps every node’s children in place. Log the inorder traversal of the inverted BST [4, 2, 7, 1, 3, 6, 9]. Expected reversed order.
hints: Recurse left and right first, THEN assign the swapped results.
Inorder of a BST is sorted ASC; after inversion it becomes sorted DESC.
